title: Pesto
description:
Pesto sauce is one of those remarkably easy and remarkably tasty preparations that make it a favorite of ours, and many others. How can you go wrong with the starting ingredients of garlic, oil, and parmesan cheese?
In the old days, making it would signal the beginning of summer, with the availability of fresh basil. But today – hurray! – you can get fresh basil plants throughout the year, so this can be enjoyed all the time.
Pasta is the usual canvas for Pesto, but because it also freezes well, some Pesto can be popped out at a moment’s notice for all kinds of other combinations – a couple of dollops on a roasted tomato soup, mixed with a little mayo for a potato salad, or a little sauce for grilled chicken or fish, or as a topping for a sandwich, such as turkey, provolone, and pesto panini, or a grilled chicken breast “burger” with pesto mayonnaise, tomato, and melted cheese.
Pesto
ingredients: 1 cup pinolas or pine nuts, or
directions: Drop the garlic cloves one at a time into a running food processor to get them finely minced. Turn off and scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Add the basil and nuts to the processor bowl and coarsely chop.
Then, with the motor running, add the olive oil in a steady stream. Turn off.
Cook the pasta in boiling, salted water until al dente (time varies with the kind of pasta you’re using, so occasionally lift a strand and take a bite.)
Stir 2 tablespoons of the hot pasta water and maybe some heavy cream into the pesto.
Serve warm, maybe with a little extra pepper or possibly extra Parmesan or Romano.
This is also good at room temperature.

Scrape down the sides of the processor bowl. Add the cheeses, a big pinch of salt and a generous grinding of pepper to taste. Pulse briefly to combine well. Scrape all into another bowl and cover until ready to use.
